info.name: FlashArray REST Active Directory Fleets API

params.name: continuation_token
params.description:
A token used to retrieve the next page of data
with some consistency guaranteed.
The token is a Base64 encoded value.
Set `continuation_token` to the system-generated token taken from the `x-next-token`
header field of the response.
A query has reached its last page when the response does not include a token.
Pagination requires the `limit` and `continuation_token`
query parameters.

params.name: filter
params.description:
Narrows down the results to only the response objects
that satisfy the filter criteria.

params.name: ids
params.description:
A comma-separated list of unique resource IDs. At least one resource must match
 each specified ID, otherwise an error is returned. This parameter is required
  if ids or names is not provided, but it cannot be used together with name or names.

params.name: limit
params.description:
Limits the size of the response to the specified number of objects on each page.
To return the total number of resources, set `limit=0`.
The total number of resources is returned as a `total_item_count` value.
If the page size requested is larger than the system maximum limit,
the server returns the maximum limit, disregarding the requested page size.

params.name: names
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique resource names specified.
Only one value is supported.

params.name: offset
params.description:
The starting position based on the results of the query
in relation to the full set of response objects returned.

params.name: sort
params.description:
Sorts the response objects by the specified fields. Sorting can be applied to any field name
 in the response, in ascending order by default, or in descending order by prefixing the
 field name with a minus sign (-). Multiple fields can be specified as a comma-separated
 list (e.g., sort volumes by size descending, then by name ascending). If sort is provided,
 the response will not include a continuation_token.

params.name: total_item_count
params.description:
If set to `true`, the `total_item_count` matching the
specified query parameters is calculated and returned in
the response. If set to `false`, the `total_item_count`
is `null` in the response. This may speed up queries
where the `total_item_count` is large. If not specified,
defaults to `false`.

items.docs: Displays information about the fleets known to the array.

params.name: names
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique resource names specified.

new name in the `name` parameter in the request body.

params.name: ids
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique resource IDs specified.

params.name: names

A fleet can only be deleted if the current array is the only array in the fleet.

info.name: Pure Storage Add Members to a Fleet

params.name: fleet_ids
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique Fleet IDs specified.
This query currently accepts only 1 ID.

params.name: fleet_names
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique Fleet names specified.
Enter multiple names in comma-separated format.
For example, `name01,name02`.
This query currently accepts only 1 name.

items.docs:
Adds arrays to an existing fleet. This API needs to be run from the array that's joining the
fleet.

To add the current array to the fleet, specify its own array `id` or `name`,
as well as the `fleet key` generated on any array already in the fleet.
`resource_type` is `remote-arrays`.
The array's `ID` and `name` can be retrieved with a call to `GET /arrays` on the array.

params.name: member_ids
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique member IDs specified.
Enter multiple member IDs in comma-separated format.
The `member_ids` or `member_names` parameter is required, but they cannot be set together.

params.name: member_names
params.description:
Performs the operation on the unique member name specified.
Examples of members include volumes, hosts, host groups, and directories.
Enter multiple names in comma-separated format. For example, `vol01,vol02`.

params.name: unreachable
params.description:
If set to `true`, allows a one-sided disconnect when the connection
status is `connecting` instead of `connected` or `partially connected`.
If set to `false`, it works just like normal coordinated disconnect.
If not specified, defaults to `false`.

items.docs:
Deletes the specified array(s) from the fleet.
Note that this will only succeed if the array(s) to be removed are not making use of any fleet
resources.
